issues.legal_issue: An accused who relies on an alibi must establish that the accused could not have been present at the occurrence, and a rejection of the alibi is not disturbed on special-leave appeal absent a cogent ground to re-examine the evidence.
material_facts: The accused relied on evidence of medical examinations and an operation, but the evidence did not specify their timing sufficiently to establish that he could not have been at the scene.
A witness who testified that the accused had rented a room could not say whether he had seen the accused around the time of the occurrence.
The trial court rejected the alibi and the High Court upheld that finding; the Supreme Court found no infirmity warranting re-examination.
issues.conclusion: The accused did not discharge the burden of establishing the alibi, and there was no cogent ground to interfere with the concurrent rejection of it.
issues.legal_principle: The burden of establishing an alibi rests on the accused. On a special-leave appeal, the Court will not re-examine the evidence underlying concurrent findings where no cogent ground or infirmity justifies interference. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_from_conviction and alibi_claimed and defence_evidence_did_not_exclude_presence and lower_courts_rejected_alibi

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_conviction: The matter is an appeal by special leave from a criminal conviction.
predicates.alibi_claimed: The accused asserted that the accused was elsewhere and could not have been present at the occurrence.
predicates.defence_evidence_did_not_exclude_presenc: The defence evidence did not establish that the accused could not have been present at the occurrence.
predicates.lower_courts_rejected_alibi: The lower courts rejected the accused's alibi.

issues.definition: When an accused appealing a conviction by special leave relies on an alibi that the evidence does not establish and the lower courts have rejected, that rejection is left undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A member of an unlawful assembly whose common object develops at the scene and who remains a member of the assembly may be held liable for an offence committed in pursuit of that object without proof of that member's individual overt act.
material_facts: The common object developed at the scene when persons came to protest against the harvesting of paddy.
The appellants remained members of the assembly after its common object developed.
The High Court found that most appellants committed overt acts and assaulted the victims, and that the appellants were not merely passive or innocent spectators.
The appellants challenged their convictions on the ground that no individual overt act had been proved against some of them.
issues.conclusion: The convictions under Section 326 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code were sustainable despite the absence of proof of an individual overt act by every appellant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, a member of an unlawful assembly may be liable for an offence committed in prosecution of the assembly's common object where the member was part of the assembly sharing that object. Proof of a separate overt act by every member is not required in the circumstances found here. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction_for_group_offence and unlawful_assembly_common_object_developed_at_scene and accused_remained_member_of_assembly and assembly_members_committed_assault and accused_was_not_passive_spectator

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_for_group_offence: The matter is an appeal from a conviction based on an offence committed by members of a group.
predicates.unlawful_assembly_common_object_develope: The unlawful assembly's common object developed at the scene of the occurrence.
predicates.accused_remained_member_of_assembly: The accused continued as a member of the assembly after its common object developed.
predicates.assembly_members_committed_assault: Members of the assembly committed an assault in pursuit of its common object.
predicates.accused_was_not_passive_spectator: The accused was not merely a passive or innocent spectator at the occurrence.

issues.definition: When an accused appealing a group-offence conviction remained in an assembly after its common object developed at the scene, members committed an assault in pursuit of that object, and the accused was not a passive spectator, liability may be sustained without proof of that accused's individual overt act.
